task_language: put the frying pan on top of the cabinet

subtasks.name: pick(frying_pan)
subtasks.outcome: never attempted: gripper never approaches the pan; it picks the white bowl instead

behaviour_summary: pi0 picks the small white bowl (step ~67), carries it back toward the robot base and loses it around step 140 (it lands behind the pan); it then spends steps 160-409 hovering over the bowl near the cabinet, nudging and tilting it in failed re-grasps. The frying pan is never touched.

failures.mode_definition: pi0 approaches, grasps and manipulates a non-instructed object in the scene instead of the instructed target object.
hl_remedy: RETREAT(dz=+0.05) then lower and open gripper to set the wrong object back down near its start
REPROMPT('pick up the frying pan and place it on top of the cabinet')
WATCH(EE approaches the frying pan, 5 s)
on no approach: retry once with VERIFY of the target at pre-grasp, then ESCALATE
failures.prevention: Before allowing gripper closure, VERIFY the object under the gripper is the instructed target (pre-grasp identity check); HALT as soon as the EE descends over a non-target object for 2 frames.
failures.observation: Steps 0-47 the arm lowers near its base. By step 53 the gripper is over the white bowl, closes on it at ~67 and lifts it by 93. The pan (large, handle to the left) is never approached in the whole episode.

failures.mode_definition: An object that was grasped and lifted falls out of the gripper while being carried, before reaching any destination.
failures.rl_success_check: white bowl lifted >5 cm and still in the gripper after a 15 cm transport
failures.observation: Bowl held under the gripper at 93-133 while the arm moves back toward the robot base; at 140 the bowl is in free fall/tumbling below the gripper, at 147 it rests upright behind the pan. Later re-grasps (333-387) tilt the bowl but never lift it. Recorded only as LL evidence; the object is not part of the instruction.

notes: Could not tell whether the step-140 drop was a slip or a deliberate release in mid-air (no destination nearby, so a slip is more likely). Frames 167-409 show the arm repeatedly hovering low over the bowl beside the cabinet; no contact with the pan or the cabinet top.
